chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: The 'Going Places' sequence with Louis Armstrong
summary: She describes the six-minute musical sequence, the Dandridge Sisters and the group of musicians.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Now there was a sequence in the movie, 'Going Places.' In fact, I'd been listeining to the Louie Armstrong Festival, and I was --
Radion Station WKCR, New York City, has just been playing -- how long -- something like two weeks --
Two hundred and fifty hours of Louis Armstrong -- the Louis Armstrong Festival. And I was sort of waiting to hear that little segment in the movie, Going Places, that we did.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
There was a six-minute sequence in there in which we did -- it was called "Mutiny In The Nursery."
And my selections were -- As the scene opened, I was -- there was this group of musicians and kids on a lawn of the big house, and I was a maid.

And I was upstairs looking out the window. And I sang to the tune of 'Go In and Out The Window' -- 'I better close the window, I better close the window, I better close the window, they're making too much noise.'
Then later, I come downstairs and join them on the lawn. And I said I'd better join them.
Anyway, this sequence runs for about six minutes in its own kind of nursery rhymes: "Oats, peas, beans, and barley body grow."
And everybody -- the Dandridge Sisters were in this scene: The musicians were on the lawn, but there were a lot of people in the background.
Lloyd and I and a group, The Four Tops;
*Not the pop group of Motown Records fame.

and I think one of the musicians in the group was Lester Young's brother. He played saxophone, I believe, or maybe drums. I don't know, I'm not too sure.
But anyway -- MR. HUGHES: Lee Young. MS. SULLIVAN: Lee Young, right. And they played it during the festival.
